newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice prices seen steady on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice prices seen steady on low demand.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are expected to remain steady to mixed in the next trading week after Friday's weekend and holidays for the Moslem festival of Eid al-Fitr amid low foreign demand, dealers said.
They said no major price change was likely in the next few days, but prices might rise slightly after the holidays on renewed demand, one dealer said.
He said foreign buyers were quiet in the aftermath of Pakistan's general elections on February 3, an official strike on February 5 and ahead of the Eid holidays from February 9 to 11.
Rice exports rose 83.24 percent to 217,876 tonnes worth $55 million in December from 118,899 tonnes worth $32 million in November.
In the first half of 1996/97 (July-June), rice exports rose 10.58 percent to 654,966 tonnes worth $195 million, compared to 592,300 tonnes worth $200 million in the year-ago period.
IRRI-6 prices are likely to gain slightly after a government directive to the state Rice Export Corp of Pakistan to procure rice from farmers at the rate 242 rupees per 40 kg.
